verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents official SDKs in 15+ languages (TypeScript, .NET, Java) plus React and Next.js integrations, and says flags can be managed across web, mobile, and server-side apps. Server-side and client-side SDKs are explicitly distinguished, which covers the backend, web, and mobile breadth. Consistent evaluation across SDKs is only implied, by the CLI evaluating flags "the way an SDK would" and by OpenFeature providers. missing for 10: explicit documentation of consistent flag-evaluation semantics across SDKs, named mobile SDKs (iOS/Android/React Native), independent hands-on corroboration of cross-stack consistency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: SDKs & frameworks: Choose from 15+ popular languages like Typescript, .NET, Java, and more. Integrate with any framework, including React, Next.js, and more
Manage feature flags and remote config across web, mobile, and server-side apps.
**Server-side only**: enabling this prevents your flag from being accessed by client-side SDKs.
evaluate flags the way an SDK would
